metadata.title: Only 40 rows? Export a complete follow-up list with DuckDB 2.0｜CC Subtitles
metadata.description:
Recognize when a preview omits rows and deliver a complete follow-up list from the same delivery exercise table.
For people using AI to help read CSVs who want to deliver the query together with its full results.

Original fictional delivery records and deterministic author-written programs: not real company data, customer data, public statistics, AI product responses, or an independent model before-and-after test. On 2026-10-25, we compared -agent and -no-agent with the same DuckDB 2.0.0 binary. The 40 printed rows preview the 1,200-row input; the complete 480-row handoff is the filtered result under the explicit rule: status equals delivered AND actual_days is greater than promised_days. Display omission does not mean records were lost from the query or storage.

The author deliberately shortened the actual_days column name to actual_day for the error demonstration. Agent-mode stderr contains startup text plus one valid JSON line: parse that message line, rather than treating the mixed stream as a single JSON document. We do not claim DuckDB emitted invalid JSON or caused a real third-party consumer failure. CSV, SQL, COPY, and Parquet are existing capabilities; the new feature is agent-oriented output. We did not test tokens, fees, model inference, performance, server mode, or upgrades of an existing database.

The materials include the original input, complete SQL, rerun scripts, the full 480-row CSV and equivalent Parquet, an HTML report, exact commands, and per-file SHA hashes. The original data, code, and report are CC0-1.0; DuckDB is MIT-licensed. Official writing remains the property of its authors. The CLI binary is not redistributed in this kit.

Public materials (9 commands actually run): https://github.com/x812033727/travel_scanner/tree/410633ab4addde4d4590dfecc0e138d48d072d3b/docs/videos/duckdb-agent-full-export/public-run
Complete fixtures ZIP: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/x812033727/travel_scanner/410633ab4addde4d4590dfecc0e138d48d072d3b/docs/videos/duckdb-agent-full-export/duckdb-public-fixtures.zip

📌 Chapters
00:00 A gap in the delivery preview
00:31 The source is intact; the reply omits rows
02:44 Three parcels, only one qualifies
04:38 One missing letter stops the query
07:17 Reopen the files and check every record
08:54 On-time parcels change the requirement

chapters.parcel-table-start: A gap in the delivery preview

dg2i.text: On October twenty-fifth, twenty twenty-six, I queried this delivery table on this computer.

c7uh.text: Our task is to find the parcels that need follow-up and deliver a list we can reopen.

x6vr.text: The screen shows forty rows in total, from the beginning and end, with an omission marker between them.

iaiy.text: Are these really all the records left in the table?

zni4.text: In a moment, the actual-days column name will be missing a letter.

3zp6.text: And when we save a separate file, how do we check that it contains the complete list?

a73b.text: We need to trace that output back to the source table, which still holds one thousand two hundred records.

8ex8.text: This is an original, fictional delivery exercise table. We can check every record.

ujmc.text: DuckDB's agent mode was introduced on October ninth and released with version two point zero on October twenty-first.

m4b3.text: This new mode formats tool replies more compactly and marks omitted rows in the result.

6i9g.text: A program reading the reply can use those markers to interpret what is shown.

msj7.text: Reading CSV, writing SQL, and exporting complete files were already supported.

x88h.text: In a fresh practice directory, I used two modes of the same version to process this table.

pskv.text: It does not include an AI model. This comparison does not test model accuracy or usage costs.

yqnx.text: Each record has a parcel ID, a route, and the number of days promised for delivery.

xbqa.text: Status and actual days are the other fields this follow-up rule needs.

yy8n.text: The no-agent flag explicitly selects the ordinary display format.

9gdj.text: This command uses a temporary in-memory database and skips the user's initialization file.

xd25.text: Switch the flag to agent mode, keeping the input and query unchanged.

c6hy.text: Choosing the mode explicitly keeps automatic environment detection out of the comparison.

jm9m.text: Back to the opening omission marker: where does each of these two replies show it?

t4hj.text: This query builds the same table, then sorts it by parcel ID.

zxhz.text: There is no condition selecting only a few records. That lets us identify how much of the result is displayed.

h4gg.text: The ordinary mode already lists the total row count and the number of rows shown at the bottom.

4cr9.text: That line separates the size of the query result from the number of rows on screen.

uj2p.text: Agent mode marks the gap directly: one thousand one hundred sixty rows omitted.

u5mp.text: Those rows are not displayed. They have not been lost from the query result or storage.

jumq.text: The opening preview is a way to read the reply. It is not yet a list we can hand over.

7npx.text: Now, which parcels should we keep from the complete source table?

v9hh.text: This follow-up list includes only delivered parcels whose actual days exceed the promised days.

fpcm.text: Parcels still in transit stay in the source table. They are outside this follow-up requirement.

qxv3.text: When creating the table, read the ID, route, and status as text.

abty.text: Read both day-count fields as integers, so the comparison actually compares numbers of days.

m3tz.text: This describe command lists the column names and their types.

drd5.text: Another query counts records by status, showing what kinds of records we need to evaluate.

6i82.text: Here, nine hundred sixty parcels are delivered, and two hundred forty are still in transit.

ufbq.text: The actual-days field is blank for in-transit records: there is no completed delivery duration yet.

y43c.text: Under that selection rule, should we keep this delivered parcel?

jbme.text: It was delivered. Three days were promised, but delivery actually took four.

8wey.text: It exceeded the promise, so it belongs on the follow-up list.

wg3d.text: Four minus three gives one day late.

tqeh.text: We write that calculation as a new column, so the recipient can see the difference in days.

5rfa.text: Now apply the same status condition to this in-transit record.

e77f.text: The delivered condition excludes it first. We must not fill that blank with zero days.

ewsi.text: Write the selection rule we just used into this WHERE clause.

bhcv.text: Put the subtraction in the SELECT clause as a new column. The original day counts stay unchanged.

g52d.text: Keep the ID, route, both day counts, and the difference we just calculated.

evdb.text: Finally, sort by parcel ID in ascending order, so reopening the file gives us the same order to compare.

6r94.text: This parcel was promised in three days and arrived in three days. The difference is zero.

s3h7.text: Under the greater-than rule we just used, it stays off this late-delivery list.

ntfj.text: The conditions are ready. If the actual-days column name loses one letter, how will the tool respond?

ak3j.text: First, it reports that the column cannot be found. It produces no query result.

s9ca.text: The ordinary mode can already point out this naming problem.

jsui.text: That missing letter from the opening is at the end of the actual-days column name.

xj3j.text: This query isolates the column-name problem. I inserted the typo deliberately; it is not an AI mistake.

i2fq.text: Set aside the startup text from this run, then parse the single valid JSON line that follows.

yxh7.text: The full stream mixes text with JSON, so we cannot treat it as one JSON object.

jngn.text: Read the misspelled name from the object, then look for suggested columns in its message text.

cjm4.text: I check that suggestion against the source table and find the correct spelling, including the final letter.

7g26.text: Put the correct column name we found in the source table back into this query.

2d84.text: Then restore the original conditions, selected columns, and sort order, ready to export the same list.

rw48.text: The column name is fixed. Will the reply's short preview also cut off the saved file?

epd8.text: Place that complete query inside COPY's parentheses.

tdtg.text: Keep the selection rule and sorting inside. Specify the output file's location afterward.

q6db.text: No display-row limit is added between the source table and this output.

n6c9.text: We save the full result that meets the conditions, rather than copying a few lines from the reply.

kabz.text: This path sets where the CSV is written. The HEADER option keeps the column names.

5qhj.text: When reading it back, compare the column order with the SELECT list, so IDs and routes have not been swapped.

6e4u.text: Save another copy as Parquet, changing only the output format and destination filename.

nsc3.text: Keep the same selected columns and sorting inside the parentheses for comparison later.

7b9v.text: Run the complete query with this command. It writes both formats to the locations we specified.

44a2.text: To check whether the saved file was cut short, read the exported CSV directly.

j328.text: Count the data rows in the file. The header row is not a parcel.

ubxv.text: The complete follow-up file contains four hundred eighty records in this run.

ag8z.text: The preview truncation we were worried about did not carry over into this export.

6da2.text: Running the same export in ordinary mode produces the same list contents.

385u.text: This shows that the new mode changes the reply. It did not find any extra late parcels.

zdyx.text: Is the right row count enough to hand it over? Does the other format preserve every record too?

qgqv.text: To check the other format, read the Parquet file and sort it by the same parcel ID.

ineu.text: Save it as CSV again, so we can compare both complete results row by row.

dgc2.text: Run this readback query. It reads the delivered file without rewriting the original delivery table.

xqkd.text: Remember the parcel where we subtracted three from four?

xad9.text: The complete file keeps its route, original day counts, and the one-day-late difference.

6u7e.text: As we move down the IDs, qualifying records near the end of the source table are also in the full file.

wznc.text: Checking the first and last rows helps locate records. A full comparison must check every row in between too.

h579.text: To show the recipient the distribution, count by route using the same original rule.

jd24.text: Put that short summary in the report separately. It does not replace the full parcel list.

rxjg.text: Under that original rule, routes R2 and R3 each contain two hundred forty records.

mavj.text: Together, that is the same four hundred eighty records in the full file; the summary covers those qualifying records.

3dwp.text: Now we have a row-by-row answer to the opening completeness question: both files contain the same data.

dm84.text: The comparison covers more than counts: every ID, every field value, and the row order.

ezfg.text: Separately, a simple program reads the source table record by record and applies the original rule to generate the expected IDs.

ubtk.text: Those IDs also match the export, bringing the check back to the original data.

g738.text: But if the recipient now wants parcels delivered exactly on time included, can we hand over this verified late-only list?

ab37.text: No. The on-time parcels we excluded now need to be kept too.

dyhh.text: Keep the original file, then save the new requirement as a separate query.

7th9.text: Change greater than to greater than or equal to, so records with equal day counts also qualify.

98xj.text: Change the destination filename too, so the new requirement does not overwrite the original list.

g89b.text: Run the revised file with this command, saving the new output separately.

u6gp.text: How many more parcels does that changed comparison keep, and what kind of records are they?

mkfw.text: The new list has seven hundred twenty records. Two hundred forty have zero days late.

b5i9.text: The added parcels were exactly on time, so this file is an on-time-or-late list.

fqr6.text: Remember the parcel promised in three days and delivered in three days, which we left out?

me2p.text: It now qualifies because we changed the rule to include equality.

ptfc.text: Each list follows its own condition. We cannot substitute one for the other.

ha7h.text: Keep both filenames with their corresponding queries, so the recipient can choose the correct requirement.

g7bc.text: The handoff package now contains complete data files, their queries, and a readable summary.

s9qr.text: The recipient can find the full files from the report, or change the conditions and regenerate a list.

ddtv.text: The opening preview now has a complete deliverable that we can check against its rule.

wx5u.text: What kind of data list do you hand over most often?

v5pw.text: Subscribe to understand AI tools through what we build.
